title: airgap-registry-fallback-and-helm-operator-rollback-scripts
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: Customer clusters running the private installer in fully air-gapped environments reported two operational gaps: a) a broken path during image bootstrap when the primary local registry is temporarily inconsistent or partially seeded, and b) no automated safe rollback path for Helm operator-driven upgrades where hooks or CRDs can get stuck. Motivation: Provide a transparent registry fallback strategy during bootstrapping and a small, auditable Helm operator rollback facility that operators can trigger from the installer when upgrades fail to converge. This PR provides: 1) a registry-fallback controller that validates local registry indices, falls back to a second local mirror, and surfaces deterministic preflight remediation steps; 2) a lightweight helm-rollback-operator with a safe single-retry rollback job and delta-apply helper to revert chart changes atomically; 3) Terraform helper to seed fallback mirror metadata during offline registry seeding; 4) documentation and playbook updates for operators and runbooks. Implementation notes: - Registry fallback uses a small idempotent controller (registry-fallback.go) that runs during bootstrap and upgrade windows. It performs checksums against the installer index and falls back to a configured mirrored OCI endpoint if anomalies are detected. Fallback is logged, and the controller creates a sealed preflight artifact that can be inspected offline. - Helm rollback operator is intentionally minimal: it creates a rollback job that uses chart-diff to compute a reverse delta and reapplies a pinned chart revision. We added a safety gate: operator marks the release as "rollback-in-progress" and waits for readiness probes before clearing the gate. - Terraform: minor module (registry-seed/main.tf) exposes an optional fallback_mirror block so infra automation can register secondary mirrors into the installer catalog. - Security: all fallback operations respect the sealed-bundle trust boundary and verify signed indexes before any switch. Checksums and sigstore attestations are validated. - Upgrade/rollback testing harness added to perf-canary (integration entry) to simulate partial-seed and verify graceful fallback and rollback. How to test locally (air-gapped simulation): 1) Build the offline bundle (make airgap-bundle) with two local registries seeded: primary and mirror. 2) Start installer with DEBUG=1 and set FALLBACK_TIMEOUT=30s. 3) Introduce a partial seed by stopping the primary registry during bootstrap; confirm fallback controller marks fallback that is visible in logs and preflight artifact (installer/_artifacts/registry-fallback-*.json). 4) Trigger a chart upgrade that intentionally fails probe; verify helm-rollback-operator creates rollback job, delta-apply reverses the change, and the release returns to previous-ready state. Checklist: - [x] registry-fallback controller with unit tests - [x] helm rollback operator and k8s job templates - [x] terraform registry seed module change and docs - [x] integration tests that simulate partial seed and failed upgrade - [x] docs/playbook with explicit operator steps and failure triage - [x] signed-index verification and tests Notes on backward compatibility: This is additive; operators without configured fallback_mirror keep existing behavior. The helm-rollback-operator is installed only when helm_rollback.enabled=true to avoid surprise behavior. Rollout plan: - Canary in perf lab for 2 days with simulated partial-seed jobs. - Ship as part of 2024.12 private-installer patch release. Related: builds on previous offline-seeding and delta-snapshot work; complements ENG-9013 for upgrade observability.

Diego Morales (security): Ensure signed-index verification happens before any image switch. Also add a short audit event emission. -- added sigstore verification and audit event hook.

release_notes: Adds registry fallback behavior for air-gapped bootstraps, a safe helm rollback operator for failed upgrades, and Terraform helpers to register fallback mirrors. Includes docs and an integration harness for partial-seed testing.
